ELMALILI:20:10-54/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:20:10-54/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:20:10-54/r5.claim: In the phrase about producing varied plants, the discourse shifts grammatically from speaking of God in the third person to the first person.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p43/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p43/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p43/r1.claim: These four verses are God's direct insertion, not Moses's speech; the shift makes the past account address present-day Quraysh and identify their true Lord and rightful object of worship and obedience.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p43/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p43/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p43/r2.claim: The insertion informs Quraysh that the message also concerns them and asks them to recognize who deserves worship and obedience.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p43/r2.anchor: to inform the pharaohs of the Quraysh

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p43/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p43/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p43/r3.claim: The first two verses point to the being responsible for the created order; its signs reveal providence, wisdom, power, and mercy and support monotheism and judgment.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p43/r3.anchor: there are many arguments in them for men of understanding

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p43/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p43/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p43/r4.claim: Only the one who arranged the earth's provisions deserves to be regarded as Lord; nobody else has a role in them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p43/r4.anchor: only that being is worthy of being regarded as Lord

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p44/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p44/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p44/r1.claim: The first-person wording confirms that the inserted verses are God's words, not part of Moses's conversation.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p44/r1.anchor: in the first person and hence they are not part of Moses’ conversation

ASAD-NOTES:20:53#n35/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:53#n35/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:53#n35/r1.claim: Earth's ways and means include material and intellectual resources for earning a livelihood on and from the earth.
ASAD-NOTES:20:53#n35/r1.anchor: has provided you with ways and means - both material and intellectual - to gain your livelihood on earth and from it

ASAD-NOTES:20:53#n36/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:53#n36/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:53#n36/r1.claim: Azwaj literally means "pairs" but apparently means "kinds" here; Asad points to 13:3, note 7.
ASAD-NOTES:20:53#n36/r1.anchor: a term which in this context apparently denotes "kinds"; but see also 13:3 and the corresponding note 7

BURSEVI:v5p303#4/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p303#4/r5.speaker: الإمام الراغب
BURSEVI:v5p303#4/r5.claim: Al-Rāghib defines mahd as what is prepared for a child and mahd or mihād as a prepared, level place.
BURSEVI:v5p303#4/r5.anchor: قال الإمام الراغب : المهد ما يهيأ للصبي والمهد والمهاد المكان الممهد الموطأ

BURSEVI:v5p303#4/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p303#4/r6.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v5p303#4/r6.claim: Al-Kāshifī glosses the earth as spread out comfortably for sitting and making a dwelling.
BURSEVI:v5p303#4/r6.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (خوش كسترانيدكه برآن مى نشينيد ومسكن ميسازيد)

BURSEVI:v5p303#4/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p303#4/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p303#4/r7.claim: God laid many roads between mountains, valleys, and open lands so people could travel between regions, meet needs, and benefit.
BURSEVI:v5p303#4/r7.anchor: والمعنى جعل لكم أي : لأجلكم لا لغيركم طرقا كثيرة ووسطها بين الجبال والأودية والبراري

BURSEVI:v5p303#4/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p303#4/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p303#4/r8.claim: The sky can mean the celestial sphere or clouds, since anything above is called sky.
BURSEVI:v5p303#4/r8.anchor: من السمآء} أي : من الفلك أو من السحاب فإن كل ما علا سحاب

BURSEVI:v5p303#4/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p303#4/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p303#4/r9.claim: Here the water is rain; the indefinite wording indicates that only some water was sent down.
BURSEVI:v5p303#4/r9.anchor: والمراد هنا المطر وهو الأجزاء المائية إذا التأم بعضها مع بعض ونكره قصدا إلى معنى البعضية

BURSEVI:v5p304/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p304/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p304/r1.claim: The verb means bringing plants forth through water; the first-person plural shifts from third person to emphasize the act's special attribution to God, which no one else can perform.
BURSEVI:v5p304/r1.anchor: أي : أنبتنا بسببه ذكر الماء وعدل عن لفظ الغيبة إلى صيغة التكلم

BURSEVI:v5p304/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p304/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p304/r2.claim: Azwāj means kinds, named for the pairing of things that may be similar or opposed, including male and female pairs and other paired things.
BURSEVI:v5p304/r2.anchor: {أزواجا} أصنافا سميت بذلك لازدواجها واقتران بعضها ببعض لأنه يقال لكل ما يقترن بآخر

BURSEVI:v5p304/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p304/r3.speaker: الإمام الراغب
BURSEVI:v5p304/r3.claim: Al-Rāghib defines vegetation as every growing, feeding body, including trees and stemless plants; in ordinary usage it is narrowed to stalkless plants or animal fodder.
BURSEVI:v5p304/r3.anchor: كما قال الراغب النبت والنبات ما يخرج من الأرض من الناميات سواء كان له ساق كالشجر أو لم يكن له ساق كالنجم

BURSEVI:v5p304/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p304/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p304/r4.claim: The word nabāt can, in its full sense, cover every growing thing, including plants, animals, and humans; min is explanatory.
BURSEVI:v5p304/r4.anchor: ومتى اعتبرت الحقائق فإنه يستعمل في كل نام نباتا كان أو حيوانا أو إنسانا انتهى ومن بيانية

BURSEVI:v5p304/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p304/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p304/r5.claim: Shattā is the plural of shatīt, meaning scattered or diverse; it describes vegetation with different kinds, tastes, smells, shapes, and uses for people and animals.
BURSEVI:v5p304/r5.anchor: وشتى جمع شتيت بمعنى المتفرق أي : نباتات مختلة الأنواع والطعوم والروائح والأشكال

BURSEVI:v5p304/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p304/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p304/r6.claim: He prefers reading min nabāt and shattā as two modifiers of vegetation rather than modifiers of kinds, preserving the verse's end rhyme.
BURSEVI:v5p304/r6.anchor: والأظهر أن من نبات وشتى صفتان لا زواجا وآخر شتى رعاية للفواصل

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p223/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p223/r1.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p223/r1.claim: He treats the phrase as an answer following Moses’ requests to his Lord and includes it within his supplication.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p223/r1.anchor: كالجواب بعد هذه الأشياء التي سألها موسى ربه، فينبغي أن يكون ذلك كله في جملة ما دعا به.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p223/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p223/r2.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو ونافع وابن عامر
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p223/r2.claim: These readers use mihādan with an alif in this verse and al-Zukhruf.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p223/r2.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو ونافع وابن عامر: (مهادا) بالألف

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p223/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p223/r3.speaker: عاصم وحمزة والكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p223/r3.claim: These readers use mahdan without an alif in both occurrences.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p223/r3.anchor: وقرأ عاصم وحمزة والكسائي: مهدا بغير ألف فيهما .

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p223/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p223/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p223/r4.claim: Mihād is like firāsh and bisāṭ: a thing spread out; mahd is a verbal noun like farsh, and this analysis is clearest.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p223/r4.anchor: المهد: مصدر كالفرش، والمهاد مثل الفراش في قوله: الذي جعل لكم الأرض فراشا

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p223/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p223/r5.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p223/r5.claim: Alternatively, mahd may be used as a noun and pluralized on the faʿl-to-fiʿāl pattern.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p223/r5.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المهد استعمل استعمال الأسماء، فجمع كما يجمع فعل على فعال

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p223/r6.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p223/r6.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p223/r6.claim: The reading mahd can mean “possessing a cradle,” which gives the same sense as mihād.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p223/r6.anchor: ويجوز في قول من قرأ: مهدا أن يكون المعنى: ذا مهد، فيكون المعنى كقول من قال مهادا.

QIRAAT-ER:20:53:5#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:20:53:5#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:20:53:5#1/r1.claim: Mihādan means a wide bed or expanse, broadening mahd's concrete sense of cradle; the word also occurs in Quranic hell-bed imagery.
QIRAAT-ER:20:53:5#1/r1.anchor: morphological shift from mahd (cradle, singular concrete) to mihād (expansive bed/resting-place)

QASHANI:20:53-55/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:53-55/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:53-55/r1.claim: The earth made as a cradle is the bodily realm for bodily faculties, and its paths are limbs and organs such as the eye, ear, and nose.
QASHANI:20:53-55/r1.anchor: أيها القوى البدنية أرض البدن { مهدا وسلك لكم فيها سبلا } من الأعضاء والجوارح كالعين والأذن

QASHANI:20:53-55/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:53-55/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:53-55/r2.claim: Water from the spirit’s heaven means perception and spiritual assistance; from it come perceptions, actions, properties, states, and dispositions specific to each faculty.
QASHANI:20:53-55/r2.anchor: من سماء الروح ماء الإدراك والمدد الروحاني

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p342/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p342/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p342/r6.claim: After Moses' proof that God is Lord, God continues by recalling His power and unity through creating the earth, paths, rain, plants, and provision.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p342/r6.anchor: ولما ذكر موسى دلالته على ربوبية الله تعالى وتم كلامه عند قوله ولا ينسى ذكر تعالى ما نبه به على قدرته تعالى ووحدانيته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p342/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p342/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p342/r7.claim: The clause beginning alladhī jaʿala is God's speech, indicated by first-person shifts in 'we brought forth' and 'we showed him'; Abu Hayyan rejects making it an adjective of 'my Lord' as al-Hawfi and al-Zamakhshari do.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p342/r7.anchor: وإنما ذهبنا إلى أن هذا هو من كلام الله تعالى لقوله تعالى فأخرجنا وقوله كلوا وارعوا أنعامكم وقوله ولقد أريناه فيكون قوله فأخرجنا وأريناه التفاتا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p343/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p343/r1.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p343/r1.claim: Ibn Atiyya allows either Moses to quote God at 'we brought forth' or Moses to finish after the rain clause before God addresses Muhammad and all creation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p343/r1.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: يحتمل أن يكون فأخرجنا من كلام موسى حكاية عن الله تعالى على تقدير يقول عز وجل فأخرجنا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p343/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p343/r2.speaker: الأعمش، طلحة، ابن أبي ليلى، عاصم، حمزة، والكسائي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p343/r2.claim: These readers pronounce mahdan with fatḥa on mīm and a still hāʾ; the rest of the seven read mihādan.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p343/r2.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش وطلحة وابن أبي ليلى وعاصم وحمزة والكسائي مهدا بفتح الميم وإسكان الهاء، وباقي السبعة مهادا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p343/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p343/r3.speaker: المفضل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p343/r3.claim: Al-Mufaddal treats mahdan and mihādan as two verbal nouns from the same root.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p343/r3.anchor: فقال المفضل: مصدران مهد مهدا ومهادا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p343/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p343/r4.speaker: أبو عبيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p343/r4.claim: Abu Ubayd classifies mihād as a noun and mahd as the verbal noun.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p343/r4.anchor: وقال أبو عبيد: مهاد اسم، ومهد الفعل يعني المصدر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p343/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p343/r5.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p343/r5.claim: Another lexical view makes mahd singular and mihād its plural; the earth is prepared for people's use and routes to their aims are made accessible.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p343/r5.anchor: وقال آخر مهدا مفرد ومهاد جمعه، ومعنى ذلك أنه تعالى جعلها لهم يتصرفون عليها في جميع أحوالهم ومنافعهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p343/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p343/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p343/r6.claim: The pronoun in bihi refers to the water: plants are brought forth because of rain.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p343/r6.anchor: والضمير في به عائد على الماء أي بسببه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p343/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p343/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p343/r7.claim: Azwājan means kinds; the shift to first-person emphasizes that only God can produce this.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p343/r7.anchor: أزواجا أي أصنافا وهذا الالتفات في أخرجنا كهو في قوله ألم تر أن الله أنزل من السماء ماء فأخرجنا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p343/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p343/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p343/r8.claim: The best syntax makes shattā an adjective of azwājan, the noun being what is described.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p343/r8.anchor: والأجود أن يكون شتى في موضع نصب نعتا لقوله أزواجا لأنها المحدث عنها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p343/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p343/r9.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p343/r9.claim: Al-Zamakhshari allows shattā to describe plant, a verbal noun used for plants collectively, differing in benefit, taste, color, scent, shape, and use.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p343/r9.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: يجوز أن يكون صفة للنبات، والنبات مصدر سمي به النابت

ALUSI-FULL:v16p205#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p205#2/r1.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v16p205#2/r1.claim: One analysis makes God begin speaking after Moses’ words end at “He neither errs nor forgets”; the relative clause then predicates an omitted “He is,” as an explanatory resumption. The Imam says this must be certain.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p205#2/r1.anchor: كلام موسى عليه السلام قد تم عند قوله تعالى : ( ولاينسى ) فيكون الموصول خبر مبتدأ محذوف

ALUSI-FULL:v16p205#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p205#2/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v16p205#2/r2.claim: Alternatively, Moses may quote God’s words verbatim, having heard them from him; “for you” rather than “for us” supports this, and the relative may describe “my Lord,” predicate an omitted subject, or be praise in the accusative.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p205#2/r2.anchor: قد سمعه من الله عز وجل فادرجه بعينه فى كلامه ولذا قال : ( لكم ) دون لنا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p205#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p205#2/r3.speaker: ابن المنير
ALUSI-FULL:v16p205#2/r3.claim: A third analysis has Moses speak from himself, then God’s narration shift “I brought forth” into the divine first person; Ibn al-Munir favors this as subtle and closest to straightforward rhetorical shift.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p205#2/r3.anchor: وهذا وجه حسن رقيق الحاشية وهو اقرب الوجوه إلى الالتفات

ALUSI-FULL:v16p206/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p206/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p206/r1.claim: Some deny an iltifāt here, or say Moses uttered this wording unchanged when the speech was narrated.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p206/r1.anchor: وانكر بعضهم أن يكون فيه التفات أو على أنه عليه السلام قاله من عنده بهذا اللفظغير مغير عند الحكاية

ALUSI-FULL:v16p206/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p206/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p206/r2.claim: He takes the first-person plural as God's speech and ranks this reading first, nearly certain: the wording magnifies God's great act.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p206/r2.anchor: واللاولى عندى الأحتمال الأول بل يكاد يكون كالمتعين

ALUSI-FULL:v16p206/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p206/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p206/r3.claim: A second possibility assigns the plural to the community of servants, who bring out the plants by tilling; this avoids an iltifāt.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p206/r3.anchor: أو هو مسند إلى ضمير الجماعة بارادة أخرجنا نحن معاشر العبادبذلك الماء بالحراثة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p206/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p206/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p206/r4.claim: A third possibility makes Moses speak through “water,” with God's speech beginning afterward; al-Alusi ranks it below the first two.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p206/r4.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون ذلك كلام موسى عليه السلام إلى قوله تعالى : ( ماء ) وما بعده كلام الله عز وجل

ALUSI-FULL:v16p206/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p206/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p206/r5.claim: Mahd is originally a verbal noun, then a generic name for what is spread for a child; it can be a second object of jaʿala as “made,” or a circumstantial predicate as “created.”
ALUSI-FULL:v16p206/r5.anchor: والمهد فى الأصل مصدر ثم جعل اسم جنس لما يمهد للصبى ونصبه على أنه مفعول ثان لجعل

ALUSI-FULL:v16p206/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p206/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p206/r6.claim: The earth may be made like a cradle, be inherently a cradle, or be “cradled” by an implied same-root verb; the last clause can be circumstantial.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p206/r6.anchor: والمراد جعلها لكم كالمهد ويجوز أن يكون باقيا على مصدريته غير منقول

ALUSI-FULL:v16p206/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p206/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p206/r7.claim: Many read “مهادا”; al-Mufaddal treats it like “مهد,” while Abu ʿUbayd calls it a noun and “مهد” a verbal noun; some take it as a plural meaning every place is each person's cradle.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p206/r7.anchor: وقال أبو عبيد : المهاد اسم والمهد مصدر وقال بعضهم : هو جمع مهد ككعب وكعاب

ALUSI-FULL:v16p206/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p206/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p206/r8.claim: The paths are routes laid through mountains and valleys, letting people travel between regions, meet needs, and enjoy their benefits.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p206/r8.anchor: أي حصل لكم طرقا ووسطها بين الجبال والأودية تسلكونها من قطر إلى قطر

ALUSI-FULL:v16p206/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p206/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p206/r9.claim: Repeating “لكم” signals that human benefit is the primary purpose, and the first mention identifies people as the intended beneficiaries.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p206/r9.anchor: وللدلالة على أن الأنتفاع مخصوص بالانسان كرر لكم وذكره اولا لبيان أن المقصود بالذات من ذلك الأنسان

ALUSI-FULL:v16p206/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p206/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p206/r10.claim: “From heaven” may mean from its direction or from heaven itself according to some reports; “water” means rain.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p206/r10.anchor: من جهتها أو منها نفسها على ما فى بعض الآثار

ALUSI-FULL:v16p206/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p206/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p206/r11.claim: The Māturīdīs and other early authorities say God placed properties in water, but causes operate only by God's permission, leaving Him the true efficient cause.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p206/r11.anchor: كما ذهب إلى ذلك الماتريدية وغيرهم من السلف الصالح لكنه لايؤثر إلا باذن الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p206/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p206/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p206/r12.claim: The Ashʿarīs take “by it” as “at it”: water has no inherent quenching power and fire no burning power; God creates the customary effects, while al-Alusi calls the contrary charge against causal powers extreme.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p206/r12.anchor: واليه ذهب الاشاعرة فالماء كالنار عندهم فى أنه ليس فيه قوة الرى مقلا والنار كالماء فى انها ليس فيها قوة الاحراق

ALUSI-FULL:v16p206/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p206/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p206/r13.claim: The shift to “We brought forth” highlights the manifest signs of power and wisdom: a great ruler speaks in the plural of a great act and commands all things obey.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p206/r13.anchor: إلا أنه التفت إلى التكلم للتنبيه على ظهور ما فيه من الدلالة على كمال القدرة والحكمة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p206/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p206/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p206/r14.claim: The perfect verb confirms the act and the fāʾ conveys succession; some instead recast sending down and bringing forth as expressions for willing them because God does not physically perform work.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p206/r14.anchor: ويقوى هذا الماضي الدال على التحقيق كالفاء الدالة على السرعة فانها للتعقيب

ALUSI-FULL:v16p207/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p207/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p207/r1.claim: Al-Khafājī says the fāʾ makes willing follow sending down and the bāʾ makes plants follow water, avoiding redundancy; al-Alusi finds succession clearer and more eloquent, since causation is already conveyed by the bāʾ.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p207/r1.anchor: وقال الخفاجى : لك أن تقول أن الفاء لسببية الأرادة عن الأنزال والباء لسببية النبات عن الماء

ALUSI-FULL:v16p207/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p207/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p207/r2.claim: The same first-person-plural shift appears in three parallel verses, where rain is followed by fruits, gardens, or all kinds of plants.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p207/r2.anchor: وقد ورد على هذا النمط من الالتفات للنكتة المذكورة قوله تعالى : ( الم ترى أن الله انزل من السماء ماء فأخرجنا به الثمرات مختلفا الوانها )

ALUSI-FULL:v16p207/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p207/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p207/r3.claim: “Pairs” means kinds or varieties, so named because the kinds are paired and associated with one another.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p207/r3.anchor: أي اصنافا اطلق عليها ذلك لازدواجها واقتران بعضها ببعض

ALUSI-FULL:v16p207/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p207/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p207/r4.claim: “Of plants” explains and qualifies “pairs”; “شتى” means dispersed, a feminine plural of “شتيت.”
ALUSI-FULL:v16p207/r4.anchor: أي متفرقة جمع شتيت كمريض ومرضى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p207/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p207/r5.speaker: أبو البقاء
ALUSI-FULL:v16p207/r5.claim: Abu al-Baqāʾ allows “شتى” to modify “نبات,” a verbal noun whose form covers singular and plural, describing plants diverse in benefit, taste, color, smell, and shape.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p207/r5.anchor: وجوز أبو البقاء أن يكون صفة لنبات لما أنه في الأصل مصدر يستوى فيه الواحد والجمع

ALUSI-FULL:v16p207/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p207/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p207/r6.claim: God's favor includes making livestock fodder from what exceeds human need, even though people cannot eat it.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p207/r6.anchor: من نعمته عز وعلا أن ارزاق العباد إنما تحصل بعمل الأنعام وقد جعل الله تعالى علفها مما يفضل عن حاجتهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p277/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p277/r7.speaker: أهل الكوفة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p277/r7.claim: Kufan readers recite mahdan here and in al-Zukhruf as a verbal noun meaning a bed; other readers recite mihadan as a noun for something spread out, as in 78:16 as cited by the source.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p277/r7.anchor: قرأ أهل الكوفة: {مهدا} ها هنا، وفي الزخرف، فيكون مصدرا، أي: فرشا، وقرأ الآخرون: "مهادا "، كقوله تعالى: "ألم نجعل الأرض مهادا" (النبإ: 16)

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p278/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p278/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p278/r1.claim: Salaka means inserting one thing into another; God placed roads in the earth for people to travel.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p278/r1.anchor: السلك: إدخال الشيء في الشيء، والمعنى: أدخل في الأرض لأجلكم طرقا تسلكونها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p278/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p278/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p278/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says God made the roads easy for people to travel.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p278/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: سهل لكم فيها طرقا تسلكونها.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p278/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p278/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p278/r3.claim: The water sent from heaven means rain.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p278/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p278/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p278/r4.claim: At 'We brought forth,' the discourse shifts from Moses' report to God speaking of Himself.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p278/r4.anchor: تم الإخبار عن موسى، ثم أخبر الله عن نفسه بقوله: {فأخرجنا به}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p278/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p278/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p278/r5.claim: The plants are varied kinds with different colors, tastes, and benefits; each kind is a pair, some for people and some for animals.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p278/r5.anchor: {أزواجا} أصنافا، {من نبات شتى} مختلف الألوان والطعوم والمنافع

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:53/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:53/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:53/r1.claim: “Who made the earth a bed” may grammatically modify “my Lord,” serve as a predicate with an omitted subject, or be an accusative of praise.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:53/r1.anchor: مرفوع صفة ل { ربى } أو خبر لمحذوف أو منصوب على المدح

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:53/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:53/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:53/r2.claim: The Kufans read mahdan here and in al-Zukhruf, a verbal noun used as a noun meaning a cradle to lie on; others read mihadan, a noun for a spread or bed or the plural of mahd; all agree on the reading in al-Nabaʾ.

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:53/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:53/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:53/r3.claim: God placed routes between mountains, valleys, and open lands so people can travel between lands and attain their benefits.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:53/r3.anchor: وجعل لكم فيها سبلا بين الجبال والأودية والبراري تسلكونها من أرض إلى أرض

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:53/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:53/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:53/r4.claim: The water sent down from the sky is rain.

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:53/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:53/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:53/r5.claim: The shift in “We brought forth” to first-person plural narrates God's speech, highlighting the sign of perfect power and wisdom and the creatures' obedience to His will.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:53/r5.anchor: عدل به عن لفظ الغيبة إلى صيغة التكلم على الحكاية لكلام الله تعالى

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:53/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:53/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:53/r6.claim: The same first-person shift appears in other verses about bringing forth varied fruits and growing gardens.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:53/r6.anchor: ألم تر أن الله أنزل من السماء ماء فأخرجنا به ثمرات

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:53/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:53/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:53/r7.claim: “Kinds” are called pairs because they accompany one another; “from plants” and “varied” can describe the kinds, while “varied” may instead describe the plant as a verbal noun with a plural form.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:53/r7.anchor: أصنافا سميت بذلك لازدواجها واقتران بعضها ببعض

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:53/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:53/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:53/r8.claim: The plants vary in form, purpose, and benefit, with some suited to people and others to livestock.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:53/r8.anchor: أي متفرقات في الصور والأغراض والمنافع يصلح بعضها للناس وبعضها للبهائم

BIQAI-FULL:v5p22#2/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p22#2/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p22#2/r7.claim: The description of earth, paths, and rain resumes the rational proof that the creator is one and freely chooses.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p22#2/r7.anchor: الدليل العقلي على وحدة الصانع واختياره

BIQAI-FULL:v5p22#2/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p22#2/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p22#2/r8.claim: Most of earth is made like a bed, while mountains and contrasting soft and hard regions vary in whether people can settle on them.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p22#2/r8.anchor: تفترشونها , وجعل بعضها جبالا لا يمكن القرار عليها

BIQAI-FULL:v5p22#2/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p22#2/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p22#2/r9.claim: God makes routes passable across flat and rough terrain and between mountains, valleys, and sands, providing water and pasture; some places remain impassable.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p22#2/r9.anchor: سهل طرقا تسلكونها في أراضي سهلة وحزنة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p22#2/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p22#2/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p22#2/r10.claim: The differences in terrain and its useful order cannot arise from a uniform natural cause; they show one deliberate agent.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p22#2/r10.anchor: فلولا أن الفاعل واحد مختار لم يكن هذا التفاوت

BIQAI-FULL:v5p22#2/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p22#2/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p22#2/r11.claim: Rain descends from the sky, and its color and taste are directly observable signs.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p22#2/r11.anchor: { وأنزل من السماء ماء } تشاهدونه في اللون والطعم

BIQAI-FULL:v5p23/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p23/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p23/r1.claim: Moses' absorption in divine majesty makes him recognize God as the true speaker; he effaces himself and all created things, and the speech shifts to the majestic first person.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p23/r1.anchor: استغرق صلى الله عليه وسلم في بحار الجلال

BIQAI-FULL:v5p23/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p23/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p23/r2.claim: God brings forth paired, mutually resembling kinds of plants, with none entirely without a counterpart.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p23/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p23/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p23/r3.claim: The plant kinds differ greatly in color, size, benefit, nature, and taste.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p23/r3.anchor: أي مختلفة جدا في الألوان والمقادير والمنافع والطبائع والطعوم

BIQAI-FULL:v5p23/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p23/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p23/r5.claim: The world's provisions meet every creature's needs across changing conditions, for their journey to God and presentation before Him; this completeness proves God does not err or forget.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p23/r5.anchor: أبدع هذا العالم شاملا لكل ما يحتاجه من فيه لما خلقهم له من السفر إليه والعرض عليه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p23/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p23/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p23/r6.claim: Unlike God, a human maker eventually discovers defects in a product and must repeatedly work to remove them.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p23/r6.anchor: لو عمل شيئا واجتهد كل الاجتهاد في تكميله

BIQAI-FULL:v5p23/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p23/r8.speaker: ابن إسحاق
BIQAI-FULL:v5p23/r8.claim: Ibn Kathir cites a poem that Ibn Ishaq attributes in the Sira to Zayd ibn Amr ibn Nufayl.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p23/r8.anchor: عزاه ابن اسحاق في السيرة لزيد بن عمرو بن نفيل

BIQAI-FULL:v5p23/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p23/r9.speaker: ابن هشام
BIQAI-FULL:v5p23/r9.claim: Ibn Hisham instead attributes the cited poem to Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p23/r9.anchor: وابن هشام لأمية بن أبي الصلت

BIQAI-FULL:v5p23/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p23/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p23/r10.claim: The cited poem challenges Pharaoh to claim that he made earth without supports, raised the sky without pillars, set its light, brings the sun, and grows crops and grain.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p23/r10.anchor: فقولا له آأنت سويت هذه بلا وتد حتى استقلت كما هيا

DURR-FULL:v5p582/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p582/r9.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p582/r9.claim: “Pairs” means kinds: each kind of plant has its pair, such as the separate kinds of palms and grapes.
DURR-FULL:v5p582/r9.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه في قوله: {فأخرجنا به أزواجا} يقول: أصنافا فكل صنف من نبات الأرض أزواج النخل زوج صنف والأعناب زوج صنف

DURR-FULL:v5p582/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p582/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p582/r10.claim: “Of varied plants” means plants that differ from one another.
DURR-FULL:v5p582/r10.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله: {من نبات شتى} قال: مختلف

AKHFASH:v2p443#2/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p443#2/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p443#2/r1.claim: أزواجا من نبات شتى can mean varied pairs from plants, or that the plants themselves are varied; both constructions are sound.
AKHFASH:v2p443#2/r1.anchor: وقال {أزواجا من نبات شتى} يريد: "أزواجا شتى من نبات" أو يكون النبات هو شتى. كل ذلك مستقيم.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p235/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p235/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p235/r1.claim: The three sentences interrupt the Moses story; the first begins a new topic, following the Quran's practice of renewing attention by varying its subjects.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p235/r1.anchor: هذه جمل ثلاث معترضة في أثناء قصة موسى . فالجملة الأولى منها مستأنفة ابتدائية على عادة القرآن من تفنن الأغراض لتجديد نشاط الأذهان .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p235/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p235/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p235/r2.claim: The first sentence cannot be Moses' speech because the shift to We brought forth would not fit; an omitted He is the subject, and the relative clause describes the Lord implied by my Lord in 20:52.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p235/r2.anchor: ولا يحتمل أن تكون من كلام موسى إذ لا يناسب ذلك تفريع قوله : { فأخرجنا به أزواجا } . فقوله { الذي جعل لكم الأرض مهادا } خبر لمبتدأ محذوف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p235/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p235/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p235/r3.claim: Definiteness in both parts conveys exclusive attribution: the true maker of the earth is God; this primarily recalls His blessing and implies no other deserves divinity.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p235/r3.anchor: وتعريف جزأي الجملة يفيد الحصر ، أي الجاعل الأرض مهادا فكيف تعبدون غيره . وهذا قصر حقيقي غير مقصود به الرد على المشركين ولكنه تذكير بالنعمة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p235/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p235/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p235/r4.claim: Most readers read مهادا with a kasra and alif, meaning a laid-out bed or garment, or as plural of a child's bed, referring to the many regions.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p235/r4.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور { مهادا بكسر الميم وألفف بعد الهاء وهو اسم بمعنى الممهود مثل الفراش واللباس . ويجوز أن يكون جمع مهد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p235/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p235/r5.speaker: عاصم، حمزة، الكسائي، خلف
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p235/r5.claim: These readers use مهدا with a fatha and still h, meaning like a child's cradle; both readings mean God made the earth spread out and easy to travel, sit, and lie on, with rare avoidable bumps, as in 71:19–20.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p235/r5.anchor: وقرأ عاصم ، وحمزة ، والكسائي ، وخلف مهدا بفتح الميم وسكون الهاء ، أي كالمهد الذي يمهد للصبي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p236/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p236/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p236/r1.claim: Salaka derives from entering and passing through; it can be intransitive or transitive meaning to insert, often without the causative hamza, as in Quranic examples and al-Aʿsha's nail entering a door.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p236/r1.anchor: { وسلك } فعل مشتق من السلوك والسلك الذي هو الدخول مجتازا وقاطعا . يقال : سلك طريقا ، أي دخله مجتازا . ويستعمل مجازا في السير في الطريق تشبيها للسائر بالشيء الداخل في شيء آخر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p236/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p236/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p236/r2.claim: Here salaka is transitive in the sense of making paths run through the earth, a way of saying they are plentiful in every direction.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p236/r2.anchor: فأما قوله هنا وسلك لكم فيها سبلا } فهو سلك المتعدي ، أي أسلك فيها سبلا ، أي جعل سبلا سالكة في الأرض ، أي داخلة فيها ، أي متخللة . وذلك كناية عن كثرتها في جهات الأرض .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p236/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p236/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p236/r3.claim: Paths include routes formed naturally by plains and sands as well as human trails worn into roads by repeated travel.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p236/r3.anchor: والمراد بالسبل : كل سبيل يمكن السير فيه سواء كان من أصل خلقة الأرض كالسهول والرمال ، أو كان من أثر فعل الناس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p236/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p236/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p236/r4.claim: After the blessing of earth comes the blessing of vegetation through rain from heaven, subtly recalling the creation of the heavens; saying rain was sent down from the sky, as in 80:25–26, is an eloquent insertion.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p236/r4.anchor: ولما ذكر منة خلق الأرض شفعها بمنة إخراج النبات منها بما ينزل عليها من السماء من ماء . وتلك منة تنبىء عن خلق السماوات حيث أجرى ذكرها لقصد ذلك التذكير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p236/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p236/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p236/r5.claim: The shift from third-person reference to We brought forth is an iltifat: after proving God's sole creation of earth and subjection of sky, the emphatic first person shows that the forces obey Him and that plant growth follows from the elements He created.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p236/r5.anchor: والعدول عن ضمير الغيبة إلى ضمير المتكلم في قوله : { فأخرجنا } التفات . وحسنه هنا أنه بعد أن حج المشركين بحجة انفراده بخلق الأرض وتسخير السماء مما لا سبيل بهم إلى نكرانه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p239/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p239/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p239/r1.claim: Shatta is the plural of shatīt, meaning scattered or diverse; here it refers to differing forms, colors, and tastes, some suitable for people and others for animals.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p239/r1.anchor: وشتى : جمع شتيت بوزن فعلى ، مثل : مريض ومرضى . والشتيت : المشتت ، أي المبعد . وأريد به هنا التباعد في الصفات من الشكل واللون والطعم

FARRA:v2p180/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p180/r6.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p180/r6.claim: أزواجا من نبات شتى describes plants differing in color and taste.
FARRA:v2p180/r6.anchor: أزواجا من نبات شتى [53] مختلف الألوان الطعوم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47#3/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47#3/r1.claim: Moses cites concrete acts of provision that even Pharaoh could not claim, unlike abstract predicates such as power, provision, will, or knowledge that he could falsely appropriate.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47#3/r1.anchor: لو قال هو القادر الرازق المريد العالم ونحو هذا من العبارات لأمكن فرعون أن يغالط فيقول أنا أفعل هذا كله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47#3/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47#3/r2.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47#3/r2.claim: Ibn Kathīr, Nāfiʿ, Abū ʿAmr, and Ibn ʿĀmir read mihādan; it may be the plural of a cradle or a singular noun like firāsh.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47#3/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر «مهادا» بكسر الميم وبألف، والمهاد قيل هو جمع مهد، وقيل اسم مفرد كفرش وفراش،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47#3/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47#3/r3.speaker: عاصم وحمزة والكسائي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47#3/r3.claim: ʿĀṣim, Ḥamza, and al-Kisāʾī read mahdan, with fatḥ on the mīm and quiescence on the hāʾ.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47#3/r3.anchor: وقرأ عاصم وحمزة والكسائي «جعل لكم الأرض مهدا» بفتح الميم وسكون الهاء،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47#3/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47#3/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47#3/r4.claim: Salaka means to lay open or make a way, and subul means paths.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47#3/r4.anchor: وقوله سلك بمعنى نهج ولحب، و «السبل» الطرق،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47#3/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47#3/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47#3/r5.claim: The speech of Moses may end at the descent of water, after which God addresses Muhammad and, by extension, all creation with the statement about producing plants.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47#3/r5.anchor: وقوله فأخرجنا به يحتمل أن يكون كلام موسى تم عند قوله وأنزل من السماء ماء ثم وصل الله تعالى كلام موسى بإخباره لمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم والمراد الخلق أجمع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47#3/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47#3/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47#3/r6.claim: Azwāj here means kinds, and shattā describes them as diverse.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47#3/r6.anchor: و «الأزواج» هنا بمعنى الأنواع، وقوله شتى نعت للأزواج أي مختلفات،

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p292#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p292#2/r1.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p292#2/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir, Nafiʿ, Abu ʿAmr, and Ibn ʿAmir read the word as mihādan, with an alif.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p292#2/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر مهادا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p292#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p292#2/r2.speaker: عاصم وحمزة والكسائي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p292#2/r2.claim: ʿAsim, Hamza, and al-Kisaʾi read mahdan without an alif; both forms mean a bed or spread.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p292#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ عاصم وحمزة والكسائي مهدا بغير ألف والمهاد الفراش و المهد الفرش

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p292#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p292#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p292#2/r3.claim: God made roads in the earth by opening routes for people to travel.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p292#2/r3.anchor: وسلك لكم أي أدخل لأجلكم في الأرض طرقا تسلكونها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p292#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p292#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p292#2/r4.claim: Rain is the water sent from heaven; at ‘We brought forth,’ the narration shifts from Moses speaking to God speaking of Himself.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p292#2/r4.anchor: وأنزل من السماء ماء يعني المطر وهذا آخر الإخبار عن موسى ثم أخبر الله تعالى عن نفسه بقوله فأخرجنا به

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p292#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p292#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p292#2/r5.claim: The water brings forth varied plant kinds, differing in colors and tastes; each kind is a pair, while shattā has no singular of the same form.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p292#2/r5.anchor: أزواجا من نبات شتى أي أصنافا مختلفة في الألوان والطعوم كل صنف منها زوج وشتى لا واحد له من لفظه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p298#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p298#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p298#2/r1.claim: The earth and water description completes Moses' answer to Pharaoh about his Lord after an intervening clause.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p298#2/r1.anchor: هذا من تمام كلام موسى فيما وصف به ربه، عز وجل، حين سأله فرعون عنه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p298#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p298#2/r2.speaker: بعضهم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p298#2/r2.claim: Some read the word as mahdan, a resting place on which people can settle, stand, sleep, and travel.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p298#2/r2.anchor: وفي قراءة بعضهم "مهدا" أي: قرارا تستقرون (1) عليها وتقومون

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p298#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p298#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p298#2/r3.claim: God set paths through the earth for people to travel, as also stated in 21:31.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p298#2/r3.anchor: جعل لكم طرقا تمشون في مناكبها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p298#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p298#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p298#2/r4.claim: Rain brings forth varied plants, including crops and fruits of different colors and tastes, sour and sweet; some are for people and some feed livestock fresh or dry.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p298#2/r4.anchor: ألوان النباتات من زروع وثمار، ومن حامض وحلو، وسائر الأنواع.

JISHUMI:v7p4676/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4676/r4.speaker: عاصم وحمزة والكسائي
JISHUMI:v7p4676/r4.claim: Asim, Hamza, and al-Kisai read mahdan without an alif; the others read mihādan with an alif, like farsh/firāsh.
JISHUMI:v7p4676/r4.anchor: قرأ عاصم وحمزة والكسائي: مهدا بغير ألف، والباقون مهادا بالألف، وهو كالفرش والفراش،

JISHUMI:v7p4676/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4676/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4676/r5.claim: The same reading disagreement occurs in 43:10, while all readers use the alif in 78:6.
JISHUMI:v7p4676/r5.anchor: وعلى هذا الخلاف في (الزخرف)، واتفقوا في (المعصرات) (ألم نجعل الأرض مهادا) أنه بالألف.

NAHHAS:v3p41/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p41/r1.speaker: الكوفيون
NAHHAS:v3p41/r1.claim: The Kufans read mahdan; the author says mihādan is preferable because mahd is a verbal noun.
NAHHAS:v3p41/r1.anchor: وقرأ الكوفيون ( مهدا ) ومهادا ههنا أولى لأن مهدا مصدر

NAHHAS:v3p41/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p41/r2.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p41/r2.claim: Mihādan is preferable here; mahd would work only if one supplied “possessing a cradle.”
NAHHAS:v3p41/r2.anchor: ومهادا ههنا أولى لأن مهدا مصدر وليس هذا موضع مصدر إلا على حذف أي ذات مهد

NAHHAS:v3p41/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p41/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p41/r3.claim: “He made pathways through it for you” is figurative wording for making those paths available.
NAHHAS:v3p41/r3.anchor: وسلك لكم فيها سبلا ) مجاز أي جعل لكم فيها السبل

NAHHAS:v3p41/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p41/r4.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p41/r4.claim: “From the sky” means from its regions.
NAHHAS:v3p41/r4.anchor: وأنزل من السماء ماء ) أي من نواحيها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p69/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p69/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p69/r8.claim: “Who made” can be an adjective of “my Lord,” a predicate of an omitted subject, or an accusative phrase of praise.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p69/r8.anchor: مرفوع صفة لربي . أو خبر مبتدأ محذوف أو منصوب على المدح

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p69/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p69/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p69/r9.claim: The Kufan reading “a bed” treats the earth as spread like a child's bed, or as something its inhabitants spread out.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p69/r9.anchor: { مهادا } قراءة أهل الكوفة ، أي : مهدها مهدا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p69/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p69/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p69/r10.claim: “He made paths through it” means that God placed routes amid mountains, valleys, and plains.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p69/r10.anchor: أي حصل لكم فيها سبلا ووسطها بين الجبال والأودية والبراري

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p69/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p69/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p69/r11.claim: The shift in “then We brought forth” from third-person to first-person marks God's sovereign command over varied things and signals that no one else can produce them.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p69/r11.anchor: { فأخرجنا } انتقل فيه من لفظ الغيبة إي لفظ المتكلم المطاع

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p69/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p69/r12.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p69/r12.claim: Kinds are called pairs because they are coupled or associated with one another.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p69/r12.anchor: أصنافا ، سميت بذلك لأنها مزدوجة ومقترنة بعضها مع بعض

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p69/r13.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p69/r13.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p69/r13.claim: “Varied” may modify the kinds or the vegetation; the varieties differ in usefulness, taste, color, scent, and form, with some suited to people and some to animals.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p69/r13.anchor: يعني أنها شتى مختلفة النفع والطعم واللون والرائحة والشكل ، بعضها يصلح للناس وبعضها للبهائم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p69/r14.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p69/r14.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p69/r14.claim: God provides livestock with fodder left over from human needs, which people themselves cannot eat.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p69/r14.anchor: من نعمته عز وعلا أن أرزاق العباد إنما تحصل بعمل الأنعام . وقد جعل الله علفها مما يفضل عن حاجتهم

MUQATIL:20:48-53/r8.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:48-53/r8.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:48-53/r8.claim: God made the earth a spread-out resting place and laid paths through it.
MUQATIL:20:48-53/r8.anchor: فقال: { الذي جعل لكم الأرض مهدا } يعنى فراشا { وسلك لكم } يعنى وجعل لكم { فيها سبلا }

MUQATIL:20:48-53/r9.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:48-53/r9.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:48-53/r9.claim: Rain from heaven brings forth varied kinds and colors of vegetation, some for animals and some for people.
MUQATIL:20:48-53/r9.anchor: { وأنزل من السمآء مآء فأخرجنا به } يعنى بالمطر { أزواجا من نبات شتى }

NASAFI-FULL:v3p57#5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p57#5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p57#5/r1.claim: The relative pronoun alladhī may modify Rabbī, serve as the predicate of an omitted subject, or be accusative as praise.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p57#5/r1.anchor: مرفوع صفة لربي أو خبر مبتدأ محذوف أو منصوب على المدح

NASAFI-FULL:v3p57#5/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p57#5/r2.speaker: كوفي
NASAFI-FULL:v3p57#5/r2.claim: Kufans read mahdan, while the other readers have mihādan; both are words for a spread-out, prepared surface.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p57#5/r2.anchor: كوفي وغيرهم مهادا وهما لغتان لما يبسط ويفرش

NASAFI-FULL:v3p57#5/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p57#5/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p57#5/r3.claim: The earth was made a resting place, paths were made through it, the water is rain, and salk means made.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p57#5/r3.anchor: ﴿ وسلك ﴾ أي جعل ﴿ لكم فيها سبلا ﴾ طرفا

NASAFI-FULL:v3p57#5/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p57#5/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p57#5/r4.claim: The shift in fa-akhrajnā from third person to first-person plural is stylistic; alternatively, God begins speaking after Moses, or Moses says we produced the plants through farming and planting.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p57#5/r4.anchor: نقل الكلام من الغيبة إلى لفظ المتكلم المطاع للإفتنان وقيل ثم كلام موسى ثم اخبر الله تعالى عن نفسه

NASAFI-FULL:v3p57#5/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p57#5/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p57#5/r5.claim: Azwāj are kinds, nabāt is a verbal noun used for plant in singular and plural, and shattā describes diverse kinds or plants differing in use, color, scent, and shape for people and animals.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p57#5/r5.anchor: ﴿ أزواجا ﴾ أصنافا ﴿ من نبات ﴾ هو مصدر سمى به النبات فاستوى فيه الواحد والجمع

NASAFI-FULL:v3p57#5/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p57#5/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p57#5/r6.claim: A blessing is that livestock feed on vegetation left over because people cannot eat it.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p57#5/r6.anchor: ومن نعمة الله تعالى أن أرزاقنا تحصل بعمل الانعام وقد جعل الله علفها مما يفضل عن حاجتنا

QURTUBI-FULL:20:53-55/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:53-55/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:53-55/r1.claim: Grammatically, alladhi may modify “my Lord,” serve as the predicate of an omitted “He is,” or be accusative after an omitted “I mean.”
QURTUBI-FULL:20:53-55/r1.anchor: «الذي» في موضع نعت «لربي» أي لا يضل ربي الذي جعل. ويجوز أن يكون خبر ابتداء مضمر

QURTUBI-FULL:20:53-55/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:53-55/r2.speaker: الكوفيون
QURTUBI-FULL:20:53-55/r2.claim: The Kufan readers use mahdan here and in al-Zukhruf, while the remaining readers use mihādan; Abu ʿUbayd and Abu Hatim prefer mihādan because it matches “Did We not make the earth a resting place?”
QURTUBI-FULL:20:53-55/r2.anchor: وقرأ الكوفيون «مهدا» هنا وفي «الزخرف» بفتح الميم وإسكان الهاء. الباقون «مهادا» واختاره أبو عبيد وأبو حاتم لاتفاقهم

QURTUBI-FULL:20:53-55/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:53-55/r3.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:20:53-55/r3.claim: Al-Nahhas prefers the plural reading: mahd is a verbal noun and does not fit here unless the omitted word is “possessor of a cradle.”
QURTUBI-FULL:20:53-55/r3.anchor: النحاس: والجمع أولى لأن «مهدا» مصدر وليس هذا موضع مصدر إلا على حذف أي ذات مهد.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:53-55/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:53-55/r4.speaker: المهدوي
QURTUBI-FULL:20:53-55/r4.claim: Mahdan may be a verbal noun like “bedding,” or an ellipsis for “possessor of a cradle”; mihādan can be a singular like “bed” or a plural of mahd used as a noun.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:53-55/r4.anchor: المهدوي: ومن قرأ «مهدا» جاز أن يكون مصدرا كالفرش أي مهد لكم الأرض مهدا وجاز أن يكون على تقدير حذف المضاف

QURTUBI-FULL:20:53-55/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:53-55/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:53-55/r5.claim: Mihād means a bed or stable resting place on which people settle.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:53-55/r5.anchor: ومعنى «مهادا» أي فراشا وقرارا تستقرون عليها.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:53-55/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:53-55/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:53-55/r6.claim: “He made paths through it” means roads, paralleling passages in Noah and al-Zukhruf.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:53-55/r6.anchor: { وسلك لكم فيها سبلا } أي طرقا.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:53-55/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:53-55/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:53-55/r7.claim: The phrase about sending water from the sky was explained earlier.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:53-55/r7.anchor: { وأنزل من السمآء مآء } تقدم معناه.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:53-55/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:53-55/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:53-55/r8.claim: One view takes the words about bringing out varied plants as God's speech after Moses finishes; another keeps them within Moses's speech and understands the cause as cultivation, with rain as the cause of growth.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:53-55/r8.anchor: وهذا آخر كلام موسى، ثم قال الله تعالى: { فأخرجنا به أزواجا من نبات شتى }. وقيل: كله من كلام موسى

QURTUBI-FULL:20:53-55/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:53-55/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:53-55/r9.claim: Azwāj means kinds and similar forms: different classes of plants with varied pairs and colors.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:53-55/r9.anchor: ومعنى { أزواجا } ضروبا وأشباها، أي أصنافا من النبات المختلفة الأزواج والألوان.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:53-55/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:53-55/r10.speaker: الأخفش
QURTUBI-FULL:20:53-55/r10.claim: Al-Akhfash reads the implied order as “varied kinds of plants”; shattā can describe either the kinds or the plants.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:53-55/r10.anchor: وقال الأخفش: التقدير أزواجا شتى من نبات. قال: وقد يكون النبات شتى ف«شتى» يجوز أن يكون نعتا لأزواج

QURTUBI-FULL:20:53-55/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:53-55/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:53-55/r11.claim: Shattā derives from shatta, to scatter or separate; the text lists related forms for dispersing and separation.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:53-55/r11.anchor: و«شتى» مأخوذ من شت الشيء أي تفرق. يقال: أمر شت أي متفرق. وشت الأمر شتا وشتاتا تفرق

QURTUBI-FULL:20:53-55/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:53-55/r12.speaker: رؤبة
QURTUBI-FULL:20:53-55/r12.claim: Ruʾba's line about camels arriving together and spreading out illustrates the meaning “scattered.”
QURTUBI-FULL:20:53-55/r12.anchor: قال رؤبة يصف إبلا: جاءت معا واطرقت شتيتا وهي تثير الساطع السختيتا

RAZI-FULL:v22p58/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p58/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p58/r8.claim: Razi prefers that Pharaoh feared Moses’ proof would expose his falsehood before the people, so he distracted Moses with old stories; Moses declined to discuss them and resumed the proof of divine oneness.
RAZI-FULL:v22p58/r8.anchor: وهو الأظهر أن فرعون لما قال : { فمن ربكما ياموسى * موسى } فذكر موسى عليه السلام دليلا ظاهرا وبرهانا باهرا على هذا المطلوب

RAZI-FULL:v22p59/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p59/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p59/r2.claim: After the general proof covering people, animals, plants, and inanimate things, Moses offers specific proofs; the first is that God made the earth a cradle.
RAZI-FULL:v22p59/r2.anchor: لما ذكر الدلالة الأولى وهي دلالة عامة تتناول جميع المخلوقات من الإنسان وسائر الحيوانات وأنواع النبات والجمادات ذكر بعد ذلك دلائل خاصة وهي ثلاثة

RAZI-FULL:v22p59/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p59/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p59/r3.claim: The Kufans read the word here and in al-Zukhruf as “mihādan,” while the remaining readers read “mihādan” in both places.
RAZI-FULL:v22p59/r3.anchor: قرأ أهل الكوفة ههنا وفي الزخرف { مهادا } والباقون قرؤوا مهادا فيهما

RAZI-FULL:v22p59/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p59/r4.speaker: أبو عبيدة
RAZI-FULL:v22p59/r4.claim: Abu ʿUbayda prefers “mihādan” as a noun and treats “mahd” as the verbal noun.
RAZI-FULL:v22p59/r4.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة : الذي اختاره مهادا وهو اسم والمهد اسم الفعل

RAZI-FULL:v22p59/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p59/r5.speaker: غيره
RAZI-FULL:v22p59/r5.claim: Another grammarian says “mahd” is the noun and “mihād” its plural, comparing the pair to “farsh” and “firāsh.”
RAZI-FULL:v22p59/r5.anchor: وقال غيره : المهد الاسم والمهاد الجمع كالفرش والفراش

RAZI-FULL:v22p59/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p59/r6.speaker: المفضل
RAZI-FULL:v22p59/r6.claim: Al-Mufaddal says both forms are verbal nouns from mahada, meaning to prepare a bed.
RAZI-FULL:v22p59/r6.anchor: وقال المفضل هما مصدران لمهد إذا وطأ له فراشا يقال مهد مهدا ومهادا

RAZI-FULL:v22p59/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p59/r7.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v22p59/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhshari’s al-Kashshaf offers three parses for “the One who made”: predicate of an omitted subject, adjective of “my Lord,” or accusative of praise.
RAZI-FULL:v22p59/r7.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : { الذى جعل } مرفوع لأنه خبر مبتدأ محذوف أو لأنه صفة لربي أو منصوب على المدح

RAZI-FULL:v22p59/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p59/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p59/r8.claim: Razi insists it must be a predicate of an omitted subject; the other parses make it Moses’ speech, conflicting with the later shift to “We brought forth.”
RAZI-FULL:v22p59/r8.anchor: إذ لو حملناه على الوجهين الباقيين لزم كونه من كلام موسى عليه السلام ولو كان كذلك لفسد النظم بسبب قوله : { فأخرجنا به أزواجا

RAZI-FULL:v22p59/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p59/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p59/r9.claim: Calling earth a cradle means God made it usable for sitting, standing, sleeping, farming, and every kind of benefit.
RAZI-FULL:v22p59/r9.anchor: المراد من كون الأرض مهدا أنه تعالى جعلها بحيث يتصرف العباد وغيرهم عليها بالقعود والقيام والنوم والزراعة وجميع وجوه المنافع

RAZI-FULL:v22p59/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p59/r10.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v22p59/r10.claim: Al-Kashshaf explains that God made roads through the earth, between mountains, valleys, and open country.
RAZI-FULL:v22p59/r10.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) سلك من قوله : { ما سلككم فى سقر } ( المدثر : 42 ) { كذلك سلكناه في قلوب المجرمين } ( الشعراء : 200 ) أي جعل لكم فيها سبلا ووسطها بين الجبال والأودية والبراري

RAZI-FULL:v22p59/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p59/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p59/r11.claim: Razi says the discussion of water sent down from heaven has already been treated in the interpretation of al-Baqara.
RAZI-FULL:v22p59/r11.anchor: قوله : { وأنزل من السماء ماء } والكلام فيه قد مر في سورة البقرة

RAZI-FULL:v22p60/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p60/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p60/r1.claim: One proposed reading continues Moses’ speech: he says the Lord made these things and that God’s servants cultivate varied plants using the rain.
RAZI-FULL:v22p60/r1.anchor: أن يكون هذا من تمام كلام موسى عليه السلام كأنه يقول ربي الذي جعل لكم كذا وكذا فأخرجنا نحن معاشر عباده

RAZI-FULL:v22p60/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p60/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p60/r2.claim: A second reading ends Moses’ words at the mention of rain, then begins God’s own speech with the production of plants.
RAZI-FULL:v22p60/r2.anchor: أن عند قوله : { وأنزل من السماء ماء } تم كلام موسى عليه السلام ثم بعد ذلك أخبر الله تعالى عن صفة نفسه

RAZI-FULL:v22p60/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p60/r3.speaker: صاحب ( الكشاف )
RAZI-FULL:v22p60/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the shift to God’s first-person voice signals that varied things obey His command; Razi cites parallel wording elsewhere.
RAZI-FULL:v22p60/r3.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) انتقل فيه من لفظ الغيبة إلى لفظ المتكلم المطاع للإيذان بأنه سبحانه وتعالى مطاع تنقاد الأشياء المختلفة لأمره

RAZI-FULL:v22p60/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p60/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p60/r4.claim: Razi rejects making all of this Moses’ speech because the following commands to eat and graze, and the mention of human return to earth, do not suit Moses’ speech.
RAZI-FULL:v22p60/r4.anchor: لأن قوله بعد ذلك : { كلوا وارعوا أنعامكم إن فى ذالك لأيات لاولى النهى * منها خلقناكم وفيها نعيدكم } لا يليق بموسى عليه السلام

RAZI-FULL:v22p60/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p60/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p60/r5.claim: Moses could divert water to irrigate fields, but could not bring forth plants with their varied colors and natures.
RAZI-FULL:v22p60/r5.anchor: لأن أكثر ما في قدرة موسى عليه السلام صرف المياه إلى سقي الأراضي وأما إخراج النبات على اختلاف ألوانها وطبائعها فليس من موسى عليه السلام

RAZI-FULL:v22p60/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p60/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p60/r6.claim: The divine speech cannot begin only at فأخرجنا because its coordinating fa is attached to what precedes it.
RAZI-FULL:v22p60/r6.anchor: لأن الفاء يتعلق بما قبله فلا يجوز جعل هذا كلام الله تعالى وجعل ما قبله كلام موسى عليه السلام

RAZI-FULL:v22p60/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p60/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p60/r7.claim: Moses’ speech ends at لا يضل ربي ولا ينسى; God begins at الذي جعل, with الذي as predicate of an omitted subject and the shift to direct address as iltifāt.
RAZI-FULL:v22p60/r7.anchor: هو الذي { جعل لكم الارض مهدا } فيكون الذي خبر مبتدأ محذوف ويكون الانتقال من الغيبة إلى الخطاب التفاتا

RAZI-FULL:v22p60#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p60#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p60#2/r1.claim: The verse’s wording gives water a role in producing plants; this does not violate Islamic principles if God gave water its properties and nature.
RAZI-FULL:v22p60#2/r1.anchor: ظاهر الآية يدل على أنه سبحانه إنه يخرج النبات من الأرض بواسطة إنزال الماء فيكون للماء فيه أثر

RAZI-FULL:v22p60#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p60#2/r2.speaker: المتكلمون المتقدمون
RAZI-FULL:v22p60#2/r2.claim: Earlier theologians deny that water has any causal effect on the growth of plants.
RAZI-FULL:v22p60#2/r2.anchor: لكن المتقدمين من المتكلمين ينكرونه ويقولون لا تأثير له فيه ألبتة

RAZI-FULL:v22p60#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p60#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p60#2/r3.claim: Azwāj means kinds or varieties, named so because they are paired or joined with one another.
RAZI-FULL:v22p60#2/r3.anchor: { أزواجا } أي أصنافا سميت بذلك لأنها مزدوجة مقرونة بعضها مع بعض

RAZI-FULL:v22p60#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p60#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p60#2/r4.claim: Shattā can qualify the varieties or the word nabāt; nabāt is a verbal noun used for growing plants and has the same form for singular and plural.
RAZI-FULL:v22p60#2/r4.anchor: { شتى } صفة للأزواج جمع شتيت كمريض ومرضى ويجوز أن يكون صفة للنبات والنبات مصدر سمي به النابت

RAZI-FULL:v22p60#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p60#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p60#2/r5.claim: The plant varieties differ in usefulness, taste, and nature; some suit people and others livestock.
RAZI-FULL:v22p60#2/r5.anchor: يعني أنها شتى مختلفة النفع والطعم والطبع بعضها يصلح للناس وبعضها يصلح للبهائم

STUDYQURAN:20:53/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:53/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:53/r1.claim: The passage links water with plant life and is compared with other descriptions of creation and rain.
STUDYQURAN:20:53/r1.anchor: The relationship between water and vegetal life is discussed in 6:99 and 13:4

SAMIN-DURR:20:53/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:53/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:53/r1.claim: الذي جعل لكم can be a predicate of an omitted subject or an omitted object of praise; then it is God's speech, not Moses's.
SAMIN-DURR:20:53/r1.anchor: أحدهما: أنه خبر مبتدأ مضمر، أو منصوب بإضمار " أمدح " ، وهو على هذين التقديرين من كلام الله تعالى لا من كلام موسى

SAMIN-DURR:20:53/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:53/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:53/r2.claim: The following switch to “We brought forth,” commands to eat and graze, and the later creation account make those clauses God's speech.
SAMIN-DURR:20:53/r2.anchor: وإنما احتجنا إلى ذلك لأن قوله { فأخرجنا به } ، وقوله: { كلوا وارعوا أنعامكم } وقوله { منها خلقناكم } إلى قوله { ولقد أريناه } لا يتأتى أن يكون من كلام موسى

SAMIN-DURR:20:53/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:53/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:53/r3.claim: One could instead treat the passage as Moses describing God and then switching to God's first-person voice, but the author distinguishes this from the prior single-speaker shift.
SAMIN-DURR:20:53/r3.anchor: فإن قلت: أجعله من كلام موسى، يعني أنه وصف ربه تعالى بذلك ثم التفت إلى الإخبار عن الله بلفظ المتكلم.

SAMIN-DURR:20:53/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:53/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:53/r4.claim: Alternatively, الذي is an adjective of ربي; this retains a difficulty with the later first-person clauses and lack of a permissible shift.
SAMIN-DURR:20:53/r4.anchor: والثاني: أن " الذي " صفة ل " ربي " فيكون في محل رفع أو نصب على حسب ما تقدم من إعراب " ربي ".

SAMIN-DURR:20:53/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:53/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:20:53/r5.claim: He accepts making الذي an adjective of ربي despite the author's objection about the later clauses.
SAMIN-DURR:20:53/r5.anchor: وإن كان قد قال بذلك الزمخشري والحوفي

SAMIN-DURR:20:53/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:53/r6.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:20:53/r6.claim: He says Moses's speech ends at “sent water down,” and God's speech begins with “We brought forth”; the author calls this remote.
SAMIN-DURR:20:53/r6.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: " إن كلام موسى تم عند قوله { وأنزل من السمآء مآء } وإن قوله " فأخرجنا " إلى آخره من كلام الله تعالى " وفيه بعد.

SAMIN-DURR:20:53/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:53/r7.speaker: الكوفيون
SAMIN-DURR:20:53/r7.claim: They read مهدا; the other readers have مهادا.
SAMIN-DURR:20:53/r7.anchor: وقرأ الكوفيون " مهدا " بفتح الميم وسكون الهاء من غير ألف. والباقون " مهادا " بكسر الميم وفتح الهاء وألف بعدها.

SAMIN-DURR:20:53/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:53/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:53/r8.claim: The two forms may be synonymous verbal nouns; alternatively, مهاد is a noun while مهد is the action, or مهاد is a plural of مهد.
SAMIN-DURR:20:53/r8.anchor: وفيه وجهان: أحدهما: أنهما مصدران بمعنى واحد يقال: مهدته مهدا ومهادا، والثاني: أنهما مختلفان، فالمهاد هو الاسم والمهد هو الفعل

SAMIN-DURR:20:53/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:53/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:53/r9.claim: Calling earth a cradle is emphatic, or omits a possessive phrase meaning “possessor of a cradle.”
SAMIN-DURR:20:53/r9.anchor: ووصف الأرض بالمهد: إما مبالغة، وإما على حذف مضاف أي: ذات مهد.

SAMIN-DURR:20:53#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:53#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:53#2/r1.claim: شتّى is a feminine-form plural of شتيت, like مرضى from مريض; the root means to disperse, and شتان is a past-tense noun meaning “separated.”
SAMIN-DURR:20:53#2/r1.anchor: قوله { شتى }: " شتى " فعلى. وألفه للتأنيث، وهو جمع لشتيت نحو: مرضى في جمع مريض

SAMIN-DURR:20:53#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:53#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:53#2/r2.claim: Most clearly, شتى is an adjective of أزواجا meaning diverse in color and taste.
SAMIN-DURR:20:53#2/r2.anchor: وفي " شتى " أوجه، أحدها: أنها منصوبة نعتا ل " أزواجا " أي: أزواجا متفرقة بمعنى: مختلفة الألوان والطعوم.

SAMIN-DURR:20:53#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:53#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:53#2/r3.claim: Alternatively, it is a circumstantial accusative of أزواجا, allowed with an indefinite because من نبات gives it specificity.
SAMIN-DURR:20:53#2/r3.anchor: والثاني: أنها منصوبة على الحال من " أزواجا " وجاز مجيء الحال من النكرة لتخصصها بالصفة وهي " من نبات ".

SAMIN-DURR:20:53#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:53#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:53#2/r4.claim: A third analysis makes شتى circumstantial to the subject pronoun raised by the preceding adjectival phrase.
SAMIN-DURR:20:53#2/r4.anchor: الثالث: أن تنتصب على الحال أيضا من فاعل الجار؛ لأنه لما وقع وصفا رفع ضميرا فاعلا.

SAMIN-DURR:20:53#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:53#2/r5.speaker: الزمخشري وأبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:20:53#2/r5.claim: They allow شتى to modify نبات, which is a verbal noun used for plants; it then means varieties differing in use, flavor, color, scent, and shape.
SAMIN-DURR:20:53#2/r5.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " يجوز أن يكون صفة لنبات، ونبات مصدر سمي به النابت كما سمي بالنبت،

TAB-FULL:v16p85/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p85/r1.speaker: بعض من اختار قراءة ذلك كذلك
TAB-FULL:v16p85/r1.claim: Some who chose this reading preferred it because mihād names the place, while mahd names the act, as with farsh and firāsh.
TAB-FULL:v16p85/r1.anchor: وزعم بعض من اختار قراءة ذلك كذلك، أنه إنما اختاره من أجل أن المهاد: اسم الموضع، وأن المهد الفعل

TAB-FULL:v16p85/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p85/r2.speaker: قراء الكوفيين
TAB-FULL:v16p85/r2.claim: Most Kufan readers recite mahdan, meaning that God spread the earth as a cradle or bed.
TAB-FULL:v16p85/r2.anchor: وقرأ ذلك عامة قراء الكوفيين: {مهدا} [طه: 53] بمعنى: الذي مهد لكم الأرض مهدا

TAB-FULL:v16p85/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p85/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p85/r3.claim: Al-Tabari accepts both widely transmitted, famous readings as correct.
TAB-FULL:v16p85/r3.anchor: إنهما قراءتان مستفيضتان في قراءة الأمصار مشهورتان، فبأيتهما قرأ القارئ فمصيب الصواب فيها

TAB-FULL:v16p85#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p85#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v16p85#2/r1.claim: Qatāda glosses the pathways as roads; al-Tabari notes that the pronoun “therein” refers to the earth.
TAB-FULL:v16p85#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، {وسلك لكم فيها سبلا} [طه: 53] أي طرقا

TAB-FULL:v16p86/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p86/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p86/r1.claim: God describes His grace in sending rain after Moses answered Pharaoh, then says He brings forth varied kinds of plants with differing tastes, scents, and appearances.
TAB-FULL:v16p86/r1.anchor: فأخرجنا نحن أيها الناس بما ننزل من السماء من ماء أزواجا، يعني ألوانا من نبات شتى، يعني مختلفة الطعوم، والأراييح والمنظر

TAB-FULL:v16p86/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p86/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v16p86/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses “varied plants” as different.
TAB-FULL:v16p86/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {من نبات شتى} [طه: 53] يقول: مختلف

TABATABAI:20:49-79#4/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49-79#4/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49-79#4/r5.claim: The question about past generations and Moses' answer remain connected to the preceding discussion of God's universal guidance; the following signs continue it.
TABATABAI:20:49-79#4/r5.anchor: إرتباطا بما وصف الله به من الهداية العامة التي منها هداية الإنسان إلى سعادته في الحياة

TABATABAI:20:49-79#4/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49-79#4/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49-79#4/r6.claim: God placed people on earth for earthly life as provision for higher, heavenly life, like a child raised in a cradle for a nobler life.
TABATABAI:20:49-79#4/r6.anchor: فالله سبحانه أقر الإنسان في الأرض يحيى فيها حياة أرضية ليتخذ منها زادا لحياته العلوية السماوية كالصبي يقر في المهد

TABATABAI:20:49-79#4/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49-79#4/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49-79#4/r7.claim: Earth's paths remind people that they must travel a path toward nearness to God and entry into the realm of honor, just as they follow paths to worldly goals.
TABATABAI:20:49-79#4/r7.anchor: وجعل للإنسان فيها سبلا ليتنبه بذلك أن بينه وبين غايته وهو التقرب منه تعالى والدخول في حظيرة الكرامة سبيلا

TABATABAI:20:49-79#4/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49-79#4/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49-79#4/r8.claim: God sends rainwater, including the waters of springs, rivers, and seas, and brings out related but varied kinds of plants; their food guides people to God's guidance and lordship.
TABATABAI:20:49-79#4/r8.anchor: وأنزل من السماء ماء وهو ماء الأمطار ومنه مياه عيون الأرض وأنهارها وبحارها فأنبت منه أزواجا أي أنواعا وأصنافا متقاربة شتى

TABATABAI:20:49-79#4/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49-79#4/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49-79#4/r9.claim: The earth as a cradle and its paths are signs of guidance; plants, food, and grazing guide humans and livestock to sustain life, while rain and plant growth also follow guidance.
TABATABAI:20:49-79#4/r9.anchor: إشارة إلى هداية الإنسان والأنعام إلى أكل النبات

TABATABAI:20:49-79#5/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49-79#5/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49-79#5/r1.claim: The preposition in 'by it' marks causation, affirming cause-and-effect relations among cosmic things.
TABATABAI:20:49-79#5/r1.anchor: للسببية وفيه تصديق السببية والمسببية بين الأمور الكونية

TABATABAI:20:49-79#5/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49-79#5/r2.speaker: القوم
TABATABAI:20:49-79#5/r2.claim: One interpretation takes the plant pairs to mean related kinds and varieties, as exegetes explained.
TABATABAI:20:49-79#5/r2.anchor: والمراد بكون النبات أزواجا كونها أنواعا وأصنافا متقاربة كما فسره القوم

TABATABAI:20:49-79#5/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49-79#5/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49-79#5/r3.claim: Alternatively, plant pairs may mean actual male and female plants, a reality the Qur'an has brought to attention.
TABATABAI:20:49-79#5/r3.anchor: أو حقيقة الازدواج بين الذكور والإناث من النبات وهي من الحقائق التي نبه عليها الكتاب العزيز

TABATABAI:20:49-79#5/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49-79#5/r4.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:20:49-79#5/r4.claim: The shift from third person to first person plural is attributed to the grandeur of creating diverse forms and kinds of life from one water; great beings speak for themselves and their helpers.
TABATABAI:20:49-79#5/r4.anchor: قيل والوجه فيه ما في هذا الصنع العجيب وإبداع الصور المتشتتة والأزواج المختلفة على ما فيها من تنوع الحياة

TABATABAI:20:49-79#5/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49-79#5/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49-79#5/r5.claim: The Qur'an uses the same shift from God sending water to 'we' bringing out plants or fruits in three other passages.
TABATABAI:20:49-79#5/r5.anchor: وقد ورد الالتفات في معنى إخراج النبات بالماء في مواضع من كلامه تعالى كقوله

TABRISI:20:52-53/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:52-53/r4.speaker: أهل الكوفة وروح وزيد عن يعقوب
TABRISI:20:52-53/r4.claim: Readers from Kūfah, Rawḥ, and Zayd from Yaʿqūb read mahdan; the remaining readers use mihādan.
TABRISI:20:52-53/r4.anchor: قرأ أهل الكوفة وروح وزيد عن يعقوب مهدا

TABRISI:20:52-53/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:52-53/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:52-53/r5.claim: Mihād is a noun like bed, carpet, or rug, while mahd is a verbal noun like farsh; the first analysis is clearer, though mahd can be used as a noun and pluralized on the fiʿāl pattern.
TABRISI:20:52-53/r5.anchor: المهد مصدر كالفرش والمهاد كالفراش والبساط

TABRISI:20:52-53/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:52-53/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:52-53/r13.claim: Alladhī jaʿala lakum al-arḍ may be genitive as an adjective for Rabb, or nominative as the predicate of an omitted subject.
TABRISI:20:52-53/r13.anchor: يجوز أن يكون في موضع جر بأنه صفة ربي ويجوز

TABRISI:20:52-53/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:52-53/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:52-53/r14.claim: Min nabātin and shattā are successive accusative adjectives for azwājan; shattā can alternatively be accusative as a verbal noun.
TABRISI:20:52-53/r14.anchor: من نبات في موضع نصب صفة لقوله { أزواجا } و { شتى } صفة له

TABRISI:20:52-53#2/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:52-53#2/r18.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:52-53#2/r18.claim: God made the earth a spread or cradle and put paths through it for people to travel.
TABRISI:20:52-53#2/r18.anchor: أي فرشا ومهادا أي فراشا { وسلك لكم فيها سبلا }

TABRISI:20:52-53#2/r19.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:52-53#2/r19.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:20:52-53#2/r19.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains the paths as routes God made easy for people in the earth.
TABRISI:20:52-53#2/r19.anchor: وقال ابن عباس سهل لكم فيها طرقا

TABRISI:20:52-53#2/r20.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:52-53#2/r20.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:52-53#2/r20.claim: The rain God sent down from heaven is rainfall.
TABRISI:20:52-53#2/r20.anchor: يعني المطر وتم الإخبار عن موسى

TABRISI:20:53-56/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:53-56/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:53-56/r1.claim: God's first-person plural then reports that by the rain He brought out different kinds of plants.

TABRISI:20:53-56/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:53-56/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:53-56/r2.claim: The plant varieties differ in color, including red, white, green, and yellow; each color is a pair.
TABRISI:20:53-56/r2.anchor: أي مختلفة الألوان أحمر وأبيض وأخضر وأصفر

TABRISI:20:53-56/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:53-56/r3.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:20:53-56/r3.claim: Another explanation says the plants vary in color, taste, and benefit: some feed people, some are fruits, and others serve different animals.

THALABI:v6p247#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p247#2/r1.speaker: أهل الكوفة
THALABI:v6p247#2/r1.claim: The Kufans read mahdan without an alif, meaning a spread or bed; the other readers use mihādan with an alif, which Abu Ubayd and Abu Hatim prefer because 78:6 has that form unanimously.
THALABI:v6p247#2/r1.anchor: قرأه أهل الكوفة بغير ألف أي فرشا، وقرأ الباقون مهادا أي فراشا واختاره أبو عبيد وأبو حاتم لقوله: ألم نجعل الأرض مهادا

THALABI:v6p247#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p247#2/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p247#2/r2.claim: Salaka means God opened, clarified, and laid out paths through the earth.
THALABI:v6p247#2/r2.anchor: وسلك لكم فيها سبلا أي أدخل وبين وطرق لكم فيها طرقا.

THALABI:v6p247#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p247#2/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p247#2/r3.claim: God brings out varied plant kinds with different colors, tastes, and uses, including white, red, green, and yellow; each kind has a pair, some for animals and some for people.
THALABI:v6p247#2/r3.anchor: فأخرجنا به أزواجا أصنافا من نبات شتى مختلف الألوان والطعوم والمنافع من بين أبيض وأحمر وأخضر وأصفر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p419/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p419/r1.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p419/r1.claim: Abu Ali explains mahd as a verbal noun like farsh, mihād as something spread like a bed or carpet, and allows mahd to be used as a noun or as ‘having a cradle’; he considers the first analysis clearer.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p419/r1.anchor: قال أبو علي: (المهد مصدر كالفرش، والمهاد مثل الفراش والبساط، وهما اسم ما يفرش ويبسط

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p419/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p419/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p419/r2.claim: S-l-k means inserting one thing into another; God laid paths in the earth for people to travel, as in the cited verse about being put into Hell and the example of a spear entering a wounded person.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p419/r2.anchor: السلك: إدخال الشيء في الشيء يسلكه فيه قال الله تعالى: {ما سلككم في سقر}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p419/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p419/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p419/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says God made paths in the earth easy for people.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p419/r3.anchor: كما قال ابن عباس: (سهل لكم فيها طرقا)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p419/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p419/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p419/r4.claim: Because the paths stretch across and appear on the earth, the verse describes them as if they were inserted into it, by analogy with something inserted into another thing.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p419/r4.anchor: ولما كانت الطرق المسلوكة ممتدة على الأرض ظاهرة عليها جعلت كأنها مسلوكة فيها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p419/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p419/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p419/r5.claim: The water sent down from heaven is rain.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p419/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p419/r6.speaker: صاحب النظم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p419/r6.claim: The نظم scholar says Moses’ reported speech ends at ‘water’; God then speaks in the first person at ‘We brought forth,’ as the following command to eat and graze indicates.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p419/r6.anchor: قال صاحب النظم: (تم الإخبار والحكاية عن موسى عند قوله: {ماء} ثم أخبر الله تعالى عن نفسه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p419/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p419/r7.speaker: صاحب النظم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p419/r7.claim: An alternative reading attaches the whole clause to Moses: God sent rain, and the human community cultivated plants with it; without rain they would not grow, as 56:63 also attributes cultivation to people.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p419/r7.anchor: وقد قيل: إن معناه مضاف إلى موسى على تأويل: الذي أنزل من السماء ماء فأخرجنا نحن معاشر عباده

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p420/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p420/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p420/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the plants as different kinds or varieties.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p420/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (يريد أصنافا من النبات مختلفة)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p420/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p420/r2.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p420/r2.claim: Al-Kalbi says the varieties differ in color—white, red, green, or yellow—with each color itself a kind.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p420/r2.anchor: وقال الكلبي: ({شتى} مختلفا ألوانه أبيض وأحمر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p420/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p420/r3.speaker: الفراء
