WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p420/r3.claim: Al-Farra says the plants vary in colors and tastes, and explains zawj as a color and azwāj as colors.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p420/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p420/r4.speaker: الأعشى
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p420/r4.claim: Al-Aʿsha’s line uses zawj for a kind or color of brocade, supporting the gloss ‘color.’
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p420/r4.anchor: قال الأعشى (¬3): وكل زوج من الديباج يلبسه ... أبو قدامة محبوا بذاك معا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p420/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p420/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p420/r5.claim: Shattā means varied and dispersed, has no singular in the same form, and derives from shatta, ‘to scatter’; the author lists its related verb forms.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p420/r5.anchor: {شتى} معناه: مختلف متفرق، ولا واحد له من لفظه، مثل: فوضى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p420/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p420/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p420/r6.claim: Shattā can modify azwāj, meaning different colors, or modify nabāt; both constructions are possible.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p420/r6.anchor: و {شتى} في هذه الآية نعت للأزواج؛ لأن المراد ألوان مختلفة، ويجوز أن يكون من نبات

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p420/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p420/r7.speaker: الأخفش
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p420/r7.claim: Al-Akhfash considers both grammatical constructions sound.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p420/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p420/r8.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p420/r8.claim: Ibn al-Anbari notes that nabāt is collective and has no ordinary singular, like shattā; treating the words as shatīt and nabāta would make their agreement clear, while ‘different varieties of plants’ is also sound.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p420/r8.anchor: ذكر ابن الأنباري القولين فقال: (النبات يقع على جمع لا ينفرد

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:51-54/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:51-54/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:51-54/r4.claim: God made the earth a bed and made its paths easy; the water from heaven means rain.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:51-54/r4.anchor: فراشا { وسلك لكم فيها سبلا } وسهل لكم فيها طرقا { وأنزل من السماء ماء } يريد: المطر

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:51-54/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:51-54/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:51-54/r5.claim: Moses' answer ends with the rain; the discourse then shifts to God's first-person plural, bringing forth varied kinds of plants with different colors and tastes.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:51-54/r5.anchor: وتم ها هنا جواب موسى، ثم تلون الخطاب، وقال الله تعالى: { فأخرجنا به أزواجا } أصنافا { من نبات شتى } مختلفة الألوان والطعوم

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p263/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p263/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p263/r1.claim: The earth made as a cradle is like the earth spread out as a bed in two other verses.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p263/r1.anchor: قوله: {الذي جعل لكم الأرض مهدا} [طه: 53] مثل قوله: {جعل لكم الأرض بساطا} [نوح: 19] . {فراشا} [البقرة: 22]

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p263/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p263/r2.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p263/r2.claim: God made routes through the earth and sent down water for people.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p263/r2.anchor: قوله: {وسلك لكم فيها سبلا} [طه: 53] أي: وجعل لكم فيها طرقا. {وأنزل} [طه: 53] لكم.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p263/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p263/r3.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p263/r3.claim: Water produces varied kinds of plants differing in color and taste, and each kind growing on earth is a pair.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p263/r3.anchor: {من السماء ماء فأخرجنا به أزواجا من نبات شتى} [طه: 53] مختلف في لونه وطعمه. وكل ما ينبت في الأرض فالواحد منه زوج.

BAQILLANI:v1p64/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p64/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p64/r1.claim: Qurʾānic verse endings may resemble the rhyme positions of sajʿ, but that resemblance does not make the Qurʾān sajʿ.
BAQILLANI:v1p64/r1.anchor: الحروف التي وقعت في الفواصل متناسبة موقع النظائر التي تقع في الأسجاع لا يخرجها عن حدها ولا يدخلها في باب السجع

BAQILLANI:v1p64/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p64/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p64/r2.claim: Sajʿ with uneven clauses, such as two words in one section and four in another, is condemned as unbalanced and ineloquent.
BAQILLANI:v1p64/r2.anchor: وقد بينا أنهم يذمون كل سجع خرج عن اعتدال الأجزاء فكان

BAQILLANI:v1p64/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p64/r3.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p64/r3.claim: If the Qurʾān were sajʿ, opponents could answer with balanced sajʿ and claim superior eloquence; its movement between forms shows its composition follows another principle.
BAQILLANI:v1p64/r3.anchor: فلو رأوا أن ما تلى عليهم من القرآن سجع لقالوا نحن نعارضه بسجع معتدل

BAQILLANI:v1p64/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p64/r4.speaker: النظام وعباد بن سليمان وهشام الفوطي
BAQILLANI:v1p64/r4.claim: Bāqillānī argues that accepting sajʿ in the Qurʾān entails the view of al-Naẓẓām, ʿAbbād ibn Sulaymān, and Hishām al-Fuwaṭī that its composition is not inimitable and people were merely diverted from opposing it; he rejects that consequence.
BAQILLANI:v1p64/r4.anchor: ولا بد لمن جوز السجع فيه وسلك ما سلكوه من أن يسلم ما ذهب إليه النظام وعباد بن سليمان وهشام الفوطي

BURHAN:v1p130/r10.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p130/r10.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p130/r10.claim: Ṭā Hā uses وسلك لكم فيها سبلا, while al-Zukhruf uses وجعل لكم فيها سبلا.
BURHAN:v1p130/r10.anchor: فى طه ﴿ وسلك لكم فيها سبلا ﴾ وفى الزخرف ﴿ وجعل لكم فيها سبلا ﴾

BURHAN:v3p319/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p319/r6.speaker: الجرجاني
BURHAN:v3p319/r6.claim: Al-Jurjani calls the Ta-Ha passage an iltifat, taking Moses' speech to end at وأنزل من السماء ماء and God's first-person report to begin at فأخرجنا.
BURHAN:v3p319/r6.anchor: وزعم الجرجاني أن في هذه الآية التفاتا

BURHAN:v3p319/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p319/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
BURHAN:v3p319/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says first-person shifts draw attention to God's exclusive power; another explanation says they vividly present scenes of distinctive or striking acts.
BURHAN:v3p319/r7.anchor: وأشار الزمخشري 6 إلى أن فائدة الالتفات إلى التكلم

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p185/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p185/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p185/r1.claim: An unjoined قال often answers an implicit question created by ordinary conversational expectations: after an action or statement, listeners naturally ask what was said next.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p185/r1.anchor: فكأنه قيل ، والله أعلم : فما قال حين وضع الطعام بين أيديهم ؟ فأتى قوله : ( ﴿ قال ألا تأكلون ﴾ ) جوابا عن ذلك .

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p256/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p256/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p256/r1.claim: The author rejects the defense that a speaker may alternate between balanced sajʿ and non-sajʿ: uneven paired clauses make the composition disordered, which cannot describe Quranic eloquence.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p256/r1.anchor: متى اضطرب أحد مصراعي الكلام المسجّضع وتفاوت، كان خبطاً. وقد عُلم أن فصاحة القرآن غير مذمومة في الأصل

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p256/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p256/r2.speaker: الباقلاني
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p256/r2.claim: Al-Baqillani argues that Quranic end sounds resemble rhymed prose but do not make the Quran sajʿ.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p256/r2.anchor: فبَاَنَ بما قلنا أن الحروف التي وقعت في الفواصل متناسبة موقع النظائر التي تقع في الاسجاع

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p256/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p256/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p256/r3.claim: If the Quran merely used sajʿ, the Arabs would not have been perplexed and would have tried to imitate it, since sajʿ was within their ability.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p256/r3.anchor: ولو كان الكلام الذي هو في صورة السجع، منه، لما تحيروا فيه، ولكانت الطباع تدعو إلى المعارضة لأن السجع غير ممتنع عليهم

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p256/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p256/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p256/r4.claim: Allowing Quranic sajʿ entails the view of al-Nazzam, ʿAbbad ibn Sulayman, and Hisham al-Quti that its arrangement is not inimitable and opponents were merely diverted from imitation.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p256/r4.anchor: ذهب إليه (النظام، وعباد بن سليمان، وهشام القوطي)

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p233/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p233/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p233/r1.claim: The root shatt denotes separation or difference; in context shattā signals difference opposed to concord, while ashtāt signals dispersion opposed to gathering.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p233/r1.anchor: والشتُّ والشتات في اللغة التفرق والاختلاف

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p233/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p233/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p233/r2.claim: The Quran uses shattā for diverse plants, divergent human efforts, and hearts that are divided; each context gives the sense of difference.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p233/r2.anchor: ومعنى الاختلاف، المقابل للائتلاف، هم ما يعيطه سياقها

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p233/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p233/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p233/r3.claim: In the two uses of ashtāt, people emerge dispersed for judgment or may eat separately, the opposite of being gathered together.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p233/r3.anchor: على حين يؤذن السياق بمعنى التفرق، المقابل للتجمع، في صيغة أشتات

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p233/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p233/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p233/r4.claim: Al-ins and al-insan share a broad sense opposed to wildness but are not synonyms; each has a distinct nuance.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p233/r4.anchor: يلتقيان في الملحظ العام لدلالة مادتها المشتركة

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p233/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p233/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p233/r5.claim: The author says al-ins invariably appears in contrast with jinn, whose hiddenness marks the unfamiliar and separates humans from hidden beings outside familiar life’s laws.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p233/r5.anchor: لفظ الإنس يأتي في القرآن دائماً مع الجن على وجه التقابل

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p13/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p13/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p13/r1.claim: The shift from singular address in the description to the first-person plural in فأخرجنا is iltifāt, used to refresh the listener’s attention; shifts also occur across person and number.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p13/r1.anchor: هذا يسمى التفاف ويستعمل لتطرية نشاط السامع وقد ورد في القرآن كثيراً

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p464/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p464/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p464/r1.claim: The shift from singular/third-person wording to first-person plural in فأخرجنا is iltifāt, a device used to refresh the listener's attention; the Quran uses shifts among person and number frequently.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p464/r1.anchor: يلتفت من الغائب إلى الحاضر ومن الجمع إلى الإفراد ومن الغائب إلى المتكلم

IBNMUJAHID:v1p417/r6.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p417/r6.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر
IBNMUJAHID:v1p417/r6.claim: These readers use مهدا with alif throughout the Qurʾān; ʿĀṣim, Hamza, and al-Kisāʾī omit it in Ṭā Hā and al-Zukhruf.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p417/r6.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر ﴿ مهدا ﴾ بالألف فى كل القرآن

IBNMUJAHID:v1p79#2/r1.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p79#2/r1.speaker: الفضل بن الحسن
IBNMUJAHID:v1p79#2/r1.claim: One genealogy gives Abu Amr as Ibn Ammar ibn al-Aryan, with an alternate lineage spelling through Ibn Jalhamah ibn Hajar.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p79#2/r1.anchor: أخبرني بنسبه الفضل بن الحسن بن عبد الله قال حدثنا روح بن عبد المؤمن

IBNMUJAHID:v1p79#2/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p79#2/r2.speaker: أبو عمرو
IBNMUJAHID:v1p79#2/r2.anchor: سألت أبا عمرو ما اسمك فقال زبان

IBNMUJAHID:v1p79#2/r3.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p79#2/r3.speaker: عبد الوارث
IBNMUJAHID:v1p79#2/r3.claim: Abd al-Warith gives Abu Amr's name as al-Aryan.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p79#2/r3.anchor: وقال عبد الوارث اسم أبي عمرو العريان

IBNMUJAHID:v1p79#2/r4.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p79#2/r4.speaker: اليزيدي
IBNMUJAHID:v1p79#2/r4.claim: Al-Yazidi gives Abu Amr's name as al-Aryan ibn al-Ala.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p79#2/r4.anchor: قال اسم أبي عمرو العريان بن العلاء

IBNMUJAHID:v1p79#2/r5.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p79#2/r5.speaker: أبو زيد
IBNMUJAHID:v1p79#2/r5.claim: Abu Zayd says Abu Amr had no name beyond his kunya; Abu Sufyan likewise had no other name, and Abu Amr was the elder brother.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p79#2/r5.anchor: عن أبي زيد اسم أبي عمرو بن العلاء أبو عمرو لا اسم له غيره وأبو سفيان بن العلاء أخوه

IBNMUJAHID:v1p79#2/r6.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p79#2/r6.speaker: أبو عمرو
IBNMUJAHID:v1p79#2/r6.claim: Abu Amr says he was already a leading authority while al-Hasan al-Basri was alive; another report dates al-Hasan's death to 110 AH.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p79#2/r6.anchor: سمعت أبا عمرو يقول كنت رأسا والحسن حي

IBNMUJAHID:v1p79#2/r7.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p79#2/r7.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء
IBNMUJAHID:v1p79#2/r7.claim: When asked whether he was Arab or a client, Abu Amr answered that his lineage was in Mazin and his clientage with Banu al-Anbar.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p79#2/r7.anchor: مر أبو عمرو بن العلاء بمجلس قوم وهو على بغلة له فقال رجل

IBNMUJAHID:v1p79#2/r8.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p79#2/r8.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNMUJAHID:v1p79#2/r8.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr saw Abu Amr sitting with young men and urged him to keep company with elders.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p79#2/r8.anchor: رآني سعيد بن جبير وأنا جالس مع الشباب فقال ما يجلسك مع الشباب

IBNMUJAHID:v1p79#2/r9.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p79#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNMUJAHID:v1p79#2/r9.claim: Ibn Mujahid portrays Abu Amr as the era's leading reader and Arabist, grounded in transmitted practice, modest, and following the Hijazi reading tradition.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p79#2/r9.anchor: وكان مقدما في عصره عالما بالقراءة ووجوهها قدوة في العلم باللغة إمام الناس في العربية

NASHR:v2p319#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p319#2/r6.speaker: الكوفيون
NASHR:v2p319#2/r6.claim: In الأرض مهادا in Taha and al-Zukhruf, the Kufans use fatḥa on mīm and a quiescent hāʾ without alif; the others use kasra on mīm, fatḥa on hāʾ, and a following alif. Ibn Mihran's report from Rawh is an error.
NASHR:v2p319#2/r6.anchor: فقرأ الكوفيون بفتح الميم، وإسكان الهاء من غير ألف

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p10#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p10#2/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p10#2/r1.claim: Jundub reports the Prophet warning against explaining the Quran by personal opinion; al-Tirmidhi calls this report gharīb and notes that some scholars criticized Suhayl.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p10#2/r1.anchor: عن جندب؛ أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p10#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p10#2/r2.speaker: الترمذي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p10#2/r2.claim: A version says even an interpretation that happens to be right is still an error; al-Tirmidhi, Abu Dawud, and al-Nasa'i transmit this wording from Suhayl ibn Abi Hazm.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p10#2/r2.anchor: وقد روى هذا الحديث أبو داود، والترمذي، والنسائي من حديث سهيل بن أبي حزم القطعي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p10#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p10#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p10#2/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir says a person who reaches the right meaning by unsupported opinion still errs by speaking without knowledge and using an unauthorized method; this is less blameworthy than reaching a wrong ruling.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p10#2/r3.anchor: قد تكلف ما لا علم له به، وسلك غير ما أمر به

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p10#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p10#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p10#2/r4.claim: He compares this principle to Quran 24:13: accusers are called liars for speaking without witnesses, even if their accusation happened to be true.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p10#2/r4.anchor: فإذ لم يأتوا بالشهداء فأولئك عند الله هم الكاذبون

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p10#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p10#2/r5.speaker: أبو بكر الصديق
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p10#2/r5.claim: Abu Bakr said he would have no refuge on earth or in heaven if he said about God's Book what he did not know, illustrating the early scholars' caution.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p10#2/r5.anchor: قال أبو بكر الصديق، رضي الله عنه: أي أرض تقلني وأي سماء تظلني؟

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p34/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p34/r1.speaker: هشام بن محمد بن السائب الكلبي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p34/r1.claim: Hisham al-Kalbi and others say Bishr ibn Abd al-Malik learned writing at al-Anbar, then brought it to Mecca; Harb ibn Umayya and his son Sufyan taught him, Umar learned from Harb, and Muawiya from Sufyan.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p34/r1.anchor: بشر بن عبد الملك أكيدر دومة تعلم الخط من الأنبار، ثم قدم مكة فتزوج الصهباء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p34/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p34/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p34/r2.claim: An alternative account says the first to learn writing from al-Anbar were people of Tayy from Baqqa, who refined and spread it through Arabia.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p34/r2.anchor: إن أول من تعلمه من الأنبار قوم من طيئ من قرية هناك يقال لها: بقة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p34/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p34/r3.speaker: الشعبي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p34/r3.claim: Al-Sha'bi says the Muhajirun learned writing from the people of Hira, who in turn learned it from al-Anbar.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p34/r3.anchor: عن الشعبي قال: سألنا المهاجرين من أين تعلمتم الكتابة؟ قالوا: من أهل الحيرة.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p34/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p34/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p34/r4.claim: The common early script was al-maktufa; Abu Ali Muqla systematized it and Ibn al-Bawwab further refined it, after which people followed their style.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p34/r4.anchor: والذي كان يغلب على زمان السلف الكتابة المكتوفة ثم هذبها أبو علي مقلة الوزير

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p34/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p34/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p34/r5.claim: Ibn al-Bawwab improved Muqla's writing method, which Ibn Kathir describes as clear and good.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p34/r5.anchor: ثم قربها علي بن هلال البغدادي المعروف بابن البواب وسلك الناس وراءه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p34/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p34/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p34/r6.claim: Because writing was not yet well developed, differences in Quran codices concerned the placement of words as a matter of orthographic craft, not meaning.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p34/r6.anchor: وقع في كتابة المصاحف اختلاف في وضع الكلمات من حيث صناعة الكتابة لا من حيث المعنى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p34/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p34/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p34/r7.claim: Abu Ubayd and Ibn Abi Dawud wrote and organized material on the orthography of the Quran.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p34/r7.anchor: واعتنى بذلك الإمام الكبير أبو عبيد القاسم بن سلام، رحمه الله، في كتابه فضائل القرآن

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p34/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p34/r8.speaker: مالك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p34/r8.claim: Malik held that Quran codices should be written only according to the orthography of the authoritative codex, while others allowed different spellings.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p34/r8.anchor: ولهذا نص الإمام مالك، رحمه الله، على أنه لا توضع المصاحف إلا على وضع كتابة الإمام

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p34/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p34/r9.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p34/r9.claim: Scholars differed over adding vowel marks and dots to codices, with some permitting and others prohibiting them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p34/r9.anchor: اختلفوا في الشكل والنقط فمن مرخص ومن مانع

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p34/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p34/r10.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p34/r10.claim: Although surah labels, verse markers, tenth divisions, juz, and hizb are common in contemporary codices, Ibn Kathir says following the early generations is preferable.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p34/r10.anchor: فأما كتابة السور وآياتها والتعشير والأجزاء والأحزاب فكثير (3) في مصاحف زماننا، والأولى اتباع السلف الصالح

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p335/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p335/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p335/r2.claim: شت means dispersed or divided; شتى is a feminine plural of شتيت, like مرضى from مريض.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p335/r2.anchor: شت الأمر شتا وشتاتا تفرق، وأمر شت متفرق وشتى فعلى من الشت وألفه للتأنيث جمع شتيت
